title: AMD Zen 7 Florence and Zen 8 Ravenna Roadmap Extends CPU Strategy to 2030
gist: A SemiWiki forum repost of an Avaq Semiconductor write-up (sourced from Trendforce, Wccftech and Phoronix) reporting AMD has extended its server CPU roadmap beyond Zen 6: Zen 7-based EPYC Florence in 2028 and Zen 8-based EPYC Ravenna in 2030. The piece notes EPYC Venice already entered production on TSMC 2nm and argues the long-dated roadmap is itself the competitive asset, giving cloud and enterprise buyers multi-year visibility, though no Florence specifications have been disclosed.

insights.claim: AMD has confirmed its EPYC server CPU roadmap through two generations beyond Zen 6, with Zen 7-based Florence products expected in 2028 and Zen 8-based Ravenna processors planned for 2030.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A named four-year-out roadmap gives modelers concrete server refresh dates for AMD share assumptions through the decade.
insights.quote: future EPYC processors will continue advancing beyond the upcoming Zen 6 generation, with Zen 7-based Florence products expected in 2028 and Zen 8-based Ravenna processors planned for 2030
insights.locator: AMD has revealed a long-term extension of its CPU architecture roadmap

insights.claim: AMD has not disclosed complete specifications for the Florence family, so the 2028 roadmap entry is a commitment to cadence rather than a disclosed technical step.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Treat Zen 7 performance assumptions as unsupported; the tradeable content here is schedule credibility, not silicon specs.
insights.quote: While AMD has not disclosed complete specifications for Florence
insights.locator: Zen 7 Florence Targets the Next Major CPU Evolution

insights.claim: Roadmap predictability is itself the product — AMD's multi-year architecture cadence gives cloud providers, enterprise customers and ecosystem partners visibility into future computing platforms, which the author treats as a key competitive advantage.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Datacenter buyers underwrite multi-year commitments on roadmap confidence — a soft moat that compounds if AMD keeps hitting dates.
insights.quote: giving cloud providers, enterprise customers, and ecosystem partners greater visibility into future computing platforms
insights.locator: Zen 8 Ravenna Extends AMD's Vision Into 2030

insights.claim: AMD's EPYC Venice platform has already entered production using TSMC's 2nm process technology, making AMD's server roadmap directly dependent on TSMC leading-edge node availability.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Confirms an anchor 2nm customer for TSMC and means any N2 capacity or yield problem transmits directly into AMD's server roadmap.
insights.quote: The company has already demonstrated its move toward advanced process technology with the EPYC Venice platform, which entered production using TSMC’s 2nm process technology.
insights.locator: Zen 7 Florence Targets the Next Major CPU Evolution

insights.claim: Zen 7 is reportedly designed around future process technology advancements rather than around a specific known node, reflecting the industry's continued push toward advanced nodes and higher performance-per-watt computing.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Architecture-follows-node means the 2028 timeline is implicitly a bet on foundry cadence — watch node slips as the leading risk to Florence timing.
insights.locator: Zen 7 Florence Targets the Next Major CPU Evolution

themes.theme: CPUs as components of heterogeneous systems

insights.claim: The Zen 6 to Zen 8 progression reflects a broader shift in which future CPUs are designed as components within heterogeneous computing systems rather than as standalone processors.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: CPU competitiveness will increasingly be judged on system-level integration with accelerators and networking, not on core counts — reframes benchmark-based analysis.
insights.quote: future CPUs will increasingly be designed as components within heterogeneous computing systems rather than standalone processors
insights.locator: CPU Competition Expands Beyond Traditional Performance Metrics

insights.claim: AMD is expanding its EPYC portfolio alongside its AI accelerator strategy to cover CPUs, GPUs, networking and software ecosystems, positioning the server CPU as one leg of a full platform rather than a standalone franchise.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Platform bundling is how AMD converts CPU share into accelerator attach — track whether CPU wins pull Instinct or networking content with them.
insights.locator: CPU Competition Expands Beyond Traditional Performance Metrics

insights.claim: AI workloads are pushing datacenter CPU requirements beyond raw processing capability toward energy efficiency, memory bandwidth and system-level integration, changing the metrics on which server CPUs are selected.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Memory bandwidth per socket becomes the differentiating spec — a lens for comparing EPYC generations against Arm-based and Intel alternatives.
insights.quote: Modern data centers require not only raw processing capability but also improvements in energy efficiency, memory bandwidth, and system-level integration.
insights.locator: Zen 8 Ravenna Extends AMD's Vision Into 2030

insights.claim: The piece's own sourcing is secondary — the write-up is attributed to an engineer from Avaq Semiconductor with information collected from Trendforce, Wccftech and Phoronix — so the roadmap dates are aggregated reporting rather than primary AMD disclosure.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Discount confidence in the 2028/2030 dates accordingly and wait for AMD's own Financial Analyst Day roadmap slide before hardcoding them.
insights.quote: Incformation collected from Trendforce, Wccftech and Phoronix
